title: Metering model for cache skips and coalesced batches
creator: Priya Shah
description: Clarify and implement an "equivalent token" metering model that cleanly accounts for tokens saved or skipped due to prefix/KV cache hits and for tokens that are coalesced across batches. This ticket scopes the metering logic changes, telemetry to validate correctness, and updates to quota and rate-limiter enforcement so customers are charged and throttled based on effective compute cost rather than naive request/token counts.
background: Recent incidents and finance audits exposed cases where token accounting diverges when: (1) requests are served from prefix or KV cache (full or partial hits), (2) prefetching is used, and (3) multiple client requests are aggregated into a coalesced serving batch. Current rules inconsistently bill for original input lengths, generated tokens, or effective model compute, causing under/over-charging and surprising quota exhaustion. Existing tickets ENG-8632 and ENG-9271 partially touch prefetch and batch aggregation billing but do not define a single canonical metric for downstream quota/rate-limit decisions.
proposed_solution: Introduce a single canonical metric 'equivalent_token_cost' (ETC) per request which is used by billing, quota enforcement, and rate limiting. ETC is computed as: ETC = model_inference_token_equivalent = (tokens_sent_to_model + model_generated_tokens) - tokens_saved_by_cache_admittance + batch_allocation_overhead. Rules: 1) Full KV/prefix cache hits set tokens_sent_to_model=0 and attribute tokens_saved_by_cache_admittance to caller. 2) Partial cache hits charge only for the non-cached suffix sent to the model. 3) Prefetch tokens that were executed but not used by the caller are charged as prefetch_cost and visible on billing but can be tagged for potential credit if prefetching policy rollback occurs. 4) When coalescing requests into a single batch, distribute shared KV/attn preparation costs proportionally by estimated ETC weight to avoid double-billing. 5) Expose an internal 'cache_admittance' boolean and numeric 'tokens_saved' on usage events so analytics and customer invoices can break down savings. Implementation will (a) add ETC field to metering pipeline emitted events, (b) update the quota/rate limiter to consume ETC instead of input_token count, and (c) add reconciliation job to migrate historical anomalies for downstream billing reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: Metering pipeline emits ETC for 100% of inference events in staging with schema documented
Rate limiter and quota checks in staged cluster use ETC and throttle behavior matches expected units under synthetic workload
Finance test dataset (500k events) shows end-to-end invoices differ from current method by <0.5% for standard workloads and corrects known undercharges for workloads heavy on prefix-cache hits
Dashboards show tokens_saved and cache_admittance breakdown per customer and per model route
Automated unit/integration tests covering full/partial cache hits, prefetch rollback, and coalesced batch allocation are added and run in CI
telemetry_queries: staging: SELECT count(*) AS events, SUM(etcs) AS total_etc FROM metering.events WHERE env='staging' AND produced_at > now() - interval '7 days'

prod-smoke: SELECT customer_id, SUM(tokens_saved) as saved, SUM(etcs) as billed_cost FROM metering.events WHERE produced_at > now() - interval '1 day' GROUP BY customer_id ORDER BY billed_cost DESC LIMIT 50
rate-limit-sim: script to replay 10k synthetic requests with varying cache-hit ratios and assert throttle rates are within expected percentiles
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flag ETC emission: start in read-only mode (emit ETC but do not let quota/rate-limiter consume it). Run for 2 weeks and compare to legacy billing metric.
2) Shadow quota enforcement: enable ETC shadow mode where the quota system computes consumption against ETC but does not enforce; collect divergence metrics for 1 week.
3) Gradual enforcement: enable ETC-based enforcement for 5% of traffic then 25% then 100%, monitoring customer-facing errors and invoice deltas.
4) Run billing reconciliation job for customers with >1% delta and issue credits where appropriate.
5) Post-rollout audit and update public docs/SDKs with ETC explanation and new billing breakdowns
